newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Parana may see later start to soy planting.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Parana may see later start to soy planting.

text.p: Soybean planting in one of Brazil's key producing states is likely to be delayed slightly due to a later than normal end to the wheat harvest, said an agronomist at the Parana State Agricultural Secretariat.
"Normally planting begins around now but so far there has been nothing as the wheat is still being harvested, particularly in the south of the country," the agronomist said.
Overall only a half of the state's wheat crop has been brought in, he added.
Any delay is not expected however to affect soybean production which is seen reaching between 6.2 million and 7.5 million tonnes against last year's 6.38 million, he added.
The traditional planting period for the state is October 15 to November 15 but planting can continue through to December.
This year between two million to 2.48 million hectares are expected to be used for soybean production, again on a par with last year's 2.3 million hectares.
The only problem may be a possible seed shortage which could cause some farmers to plant corn instead, the agronomist said.
Parana has in recent years always been the country's second largest soybean producing state, following in the footsteps of Rio Grande do Sul.

However a prolonged drought in the fourth quarter of last year in Rio Grande do Sul severely hit output there, giving Parana the chance to come out of its neighbour's shadow and take first place in the production table.

Planting in Rio Grande do Sul takes place slightly after that of Parana, reaching its peak in November and drawing to a close in the first two weeks in December, said Valdir Bisotto of the Fecotrigo cooperatives' federation.
Very early estimates are that planted area this year will increase to over three million hectares with output expected to exceed six million tonnes.
This would be a return to more normal production for the state after the drought-hit harvest of 4.4 million tonnes in 1995/96, Bisotto said.
Bisotto was hopeful this year's crop would take Rio Grande do Sul back to the top of the production league despite Parana's forecasts.
"People in Parana are very optimistic," Bisotto said.
Total soybean production in 1996/97 is expected to reach between 26 million and 27 million tonnes against 23.2 million in 1995/96.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 552 5074151
